**8B.1 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Overall read: **yes, but mostly as a policy program rather than a deep ideology**. The clearest articulated direction was a mix of **pro-growth, pro-investment, welfare/populist redistribution, democratic/rule-of-law language, and restrained regional diplomacy**. The main weakness is that the program often looked **pragmatic and ad hoc**, with some later rhetorical repositioning under pressure.

**Accepted Claims**
- **`Summit for Democracy`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-03-20** | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/summit-for-democracy-statement-2024?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848  
  Srettha explicitly tied his government to **democracy, rule of law, human rights, Universal Health Coverage, Education for All, and marriage equality**. This is the clearest statement of an articulated governing program and gives later actions a clear benchmark.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thailand says it promotes human rights for all`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-02-28** | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/statement-vfm-280224?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848  
  The government framed its public posture around **inclusive societies, dialogue, reconciliation, and rights for all**. This is explicit governing language, though still rhetorical rather than a detailed institutional roadmap.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thailand-Sri Lanka sign free trade agreement`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-02-03** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailand-sri-lanka-sign-free-trade-agreement-3291876  
  Reuters reported that Srettha signed an FTA covering **goods, investment, customs procedures, and intellectual property**, and urged private sectors to expand trade and investment. This shows a clear strategic direction toward **open, rule-based commercial statecraft**.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`

- **`Thailand and Australia deepen economic cooperation`** | **Public Relations Department, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-03-06** | https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/2078/iid/266801  
  The government publicly prioritized **trade, investment, tourism, technology, innovation, and FTA improvement**. This is strong evidence of an articulated pro-growth, pro-investment governing program.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`

- **`Thai ex-executive Pichai named finance minister, faces growth challenge`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-04-28** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thai-exexecutive-pichai-named-finance-minister-faces-growth-challenge-3401984  
  Appointing Pichai Chunhavajira, a former SET chair and Bank of Thailand board member, to Finance supports a **technocratic growth strategy**. It suggests Srettha had a coherent economic line, not just generic political messaging.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand's cabinet approves 135 billion digital-wallet handout`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-04-23** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007  
  The digital-wallet plan was Srettha’s flagship: a **universal 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million Thais**. This is revealed-goal evidence for a redistribution-heavy political program, even if it was fiscally controversial and not especially ideologically refined.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand’s flagship 14 billion handout`** | **Reuters via Yahoo News** | **2024-08-01** | https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html  
  Reuters described delays, registration snags, and criticism that the scheme was fiscally risky. This weakens the case that the program was tightly planned or evidence-led, but it still confirms a concrete governing program that could be evaluated against execution.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thailand working relentlessly to solve Myanmar crisis`** | **Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News** | **2024-05-24** | https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha  
  Srettha framed regional leadership around **reducing violence and spillover risk**, not escalation. This supports a clear strategic direction in foreign policy: restrained, stabilizing, and diplomatically managed.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`

- **`ASEAN foreign ministers' statement on Myanmar`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-04-18** | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac  
  Thailand joined a call for **immediate restraint, cessation of violence, humanitarian access, and civilian protection**. That is explicit, evaluable strategic direction in a crisis domain.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`

- **`Thailand monitored Myanmar situation closely`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-04-19** | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/weeklypressbriefing190424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e  
  The government said it had created a **special committee** and remained open to dialogue with stakeholders. That shows an operational crisis-management program rather than improvisation.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`

- **`Srettha says he respects court decision`** | **Bangkok Post** | **2024-08-14** | https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2847093/sr  
  After dismissal, Srettha said he respected the court’s decision and authority passed to the caretaker prime minister. This is limited evidence that he did not present himself as personally above institutions.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thailand’s formal 2024 IAEA statement`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-09-26** | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/iaea-09162024-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e  
  Thailand emphasized **safe and peaceful nuclear technology** and strengthening nuclear safety, security, and safeguards. This is narrower than the main domestic agenda, but it still shows a consistent rules-based policy line.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`

**Negative / Mixed Evidence**
- **`Bank of Thailand holds key rate, defies government calls for cuts`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-04-10** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-central-bank-holds-key-rate-defies-government-calls-for-cuts-3372713  
  The government repeatedly pressured the independent central bank to cut rates. This suggests Srettha’s economic program was partly **short-term political pressure** rather than a cleanly articulated long-run doctrine.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thai PM says digital wallet scheme will spur jobs and manufacturing`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-07-11** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-digital-wallet-scheme-will-spur-jobs-and-manufacturing-3514879  
  After criticism, Srettha reframed the handout as a jobs-and-manufacturing stimulus. That looks like **rhetorical repositioning**, which makes the program seem more opportunistic than ideologically stable.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Forty Thai senators seek PM’s dismissal over cabinet appointment`** | **Reuters via ThePrint** | **2024-05-17** | https://theprint.in/world/forty-thai-senators-seek-pms-dismissal-over-cabinet-appointment/2089532/  
  The Pichit Chuenban fight shows that Srettha’s governing style also included **politically connected staffing**, which complicates any claim that the program was purely technocratic or institution-centered.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand court dismisses PM over ethics case`** | **Reuters via ThePrint** | **2024-08-14** | https://theprint.in/world/thai-court-says-pm-srettha-violated-rules-on-ethics-in-cabinet-appointment/2222960/  
  The ethics ruling over the cabinet appointment weakens the claim that his governing project was consistently disciplined or cleanly bounded by institutional norms.  
  **IDs:** `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

**Search Gap**
- I did **not** find a single manifesto-like 2024 document from Srettha laying out a comprehensive ideology or regime-control theory.
- The record is better described as **an explicit policy bundle**:
  - pro-growth and investment
  - welfare/populist distribution
  - democratic/rule-of-law rhetoric
  - restrained foreign policy
- So the strongest answer to 8B.1 is: **yes, there was an evaluable program, but it was pragmatic and mixed rather than a fully coherent ideology**.
